newsitem.title: UK: MGAM fund manager says he being made scapegoat.
newsitem.headline: MGAM fund manager says he being made scapegoat.

text.p: Peter Young, the fund manager suspended last week by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), has said he is being made a scapegoat for the multi-million pound scandal rocking his bank.
In an interview with the Daily Mirror newspaper published on Thursday he said: "It looks like I'll be losing everything."
Young was suspended when MGAM, a subsidiary of German banking giant Deutsche Bank AG, said it had found "suspected irregularities" in three of its funds, two of which were managed by him.
Young, 38, denied hiding the high risks of his investment strategy from his superiors and insisted he went out of his way to detail the complex web of companies in which he bought shares.
He said that the bank did not scrutinise his work and was happy to believe he would be able to make money.
"People want to believe in magic," he told the newspaper. "They want to believe in gurus. They don't want to look inside the box because it might spoil the trick."

On Wednesday, Deutsche pledged further backing for MGAM as the British Investment Management Regulatory Organisation said investigations into irregularities in the MGAM funds, which were temporarily suspended from trading last week, could take time. ($1=.6430 Pound)
